set.n: Bashaw, Omaha railroad station burned out in the September 1894 fires (now Sarona)
set.pl: Old Omaha grade (now the Wild Rivers State Trail) at Sarona, about 15 miles north of Rice Lake, Washburn County
pinev: Moved 30 Oct 2026 off the GNIS Bashaw point in Burnett County, which has no railroad. The 1894 reports put Bashaw on the Omaha line 15 miles north of Rice Lake, with Rice Lake the next station south (Milwaukee Journal and wire reports, 2-3 Sep 1894). Measured 15 miles along the old grade from the Rice Lake depot, that lands at today's Sarona (founded 1898), so the pin is on the grade there. The distance is from the papers, so the spot is good to about 1 km. Unconfirmed placement

cd-bashaw-burned-1894.st: PLACEMENT: wire reports of 3 Sep 1894 say "the town of Bashaw, 15 miles north of here [Rice Lake], is entirely wiped out", that "the section and station houses at Bashaw were burned", and that the train crew backed up to Bashaw to take 12 refugees to Rice Lake (Little Falls Weekly Transcript, 7 Sep 1894; Indianapolis Journal, 3 Sep 1894). Railroad men said the whole stretch "from Cartwright to Bashaw and Haugen" was on fire. This is the Rice Lake to Spooner line, now the Wild Rivers State Trail. The pin was moved from the GNIS 'Bashaw' in Burnett County to the grade at Sarona, 15 miles north of Rice Lake. Sarona was founded in 1898, four years after the fire, and may be the rebuilt station under a new name. That is not proven. Look for an older depot pad along the grade near Sarona.
src: Little Falls Weekly Transcript, 7 Sep 1894, p. 1 (Rice Lake dispatch)
